description: A proposal for one small set of conventions for ducktape's cdk8s layer, scored against what the cluster needs to do, with worked examples checked against the repo and against Python cdk8s.
lede: Nine conventions to replace the 39 mechanism combinations that the generator's 199 shared helpers use today. Each was chosen against the jobs the cluster does often or will need soon, checked against what cdk8s can and cannot do from Python, and aligned with the move to admission-only Flux dependencies.
verdict:
Make the ducktape layer a thin layer of policy and wiring over the generated bindings, with exactly one shape per job. Nine conventions cover every need in the matrix, and all but one reuse a mechanism the tree already has.
- **C1 Provider kinds.** Under `providers/`, a CRD kind built more than once is a single-shot class named after the kind. Schema variants are `@staticmethod`s that return the generated struct, so a hand-built struct always fits in the same slot.
- **C2 Policy functions.** A choice this cluster makes about one kind is a function named after what it returns: `flux_kustomization`, `cnpg.cluster`, `https_route`.
- **C3 Composites.** A group of objects that repeats is a `Construct` whose objects and references are attributes: `MintedSecret`, `PrivateBucket`, `PostgresBackup`, `SettingsFile`.
- **C4 References.** A fact two objects must agree on (a Secret key, a Service port and its Pod labels, a database's app Secret) is a small frozen reference declared once by its producer and imported by its consumers. This is the one boundary change, and it needs your approval.
- **C5 Pod policy.** `pod_policy.harden()` and `pod_policy.place()` are the only functions that amend a built object. They reach cdk8s-plus, raw and CRD-embedded pod specs through one path table.
- **C6 Fleet rules everywhere.** The writer attaches them to every chart, so coverage no longer depends on an author remembering.
- **C7 Rendered directories, admission-only edges.** The writer returns what it rendered, and the Flux node derives decryption and `deletionPolicy: Orphan` from it. A `dependsOn` edge exists only for what the API server needs to admit the directory's objects (a CRD, a `Fail` webhook, a postBuild source), a synth-time check enforces that, and `wait` is off unless another node's admission depends on this one. One component is one Kustomization.
- **C8 Credentials.** A `Credential` roster entry is the only way a Secret crosses namespaces.
- **C9 Config from the consumer's model.** Our binaries render from their pydantic Settings; Terraform modules take a vars model checked against `variables.tf`.
Following cdk8s-plus's own patterns is not an option on its own: its wrappers render their specs through `Lazy`, which Python cannot put into typed binding fields, and the ways the tree emulated it (JSON-patch appends, a chart-wide singleton found by construct id) are its least-liked shapes. So every object is built complete, once, and there is exactly one post-construction amendment (C5). The design-space section shows the other options on each axis and why they lost here.
None of this is a big-bang rewrite. Each convention lands as a series of small PRs you can review as rendered diffs. The provider cleanup, the edge trim (426 edges down to 249, and 222 once #8185 lands), the writer, now writing 100 directories, and three stateless folds (181 units down to 171) have landed. Ready without a decision, cleanups first: the render-identical cores of pod policy and the namespace helper, eight more writer conversions and the ResticBackup dedupe. The edge check waits until they land. The fleet rules, graph checks, health-check derivation and glue absorption are deferred. The `wait` default and derived Orphan are postponed, and C4 and the steps built on it wait on your decision.
space_intro:
There are many ways the ducktape layer could integrate with cdk8s. The choices fall along a few independent axes: how an object gets built, how cross-cutting policy reaches it, how facts cross between objects and modules, how two-sided relationships are wired, how output and the Flux graph are organized, and where each abstraction lives.
Each axis below lists the options that were considered, with a verdict and the reason in this repo, and names the pick. The last axis compares whole-design angles, which four independent designers each developed in full before three judges scored them. Prior art from other tools closes the section.

design_space.question: How does ducktape code produce an object whose inputs are known at different points of the chart function?

options.name: Single-shot constructor
options.note: Every input arrives in one `__init__` or function call, and the object is complete when it returns. It matches the generated jsii structs, which are copied by value at construction.

options.name: cdk8s-plus fluent accumulators
options.note: `add_container`, `mount`, `env.add_variable`, `Role.allow` and `add_subjects` render at synth whenever they are called, because cdk8s-plus renders its L1 through `Lazy` internally. They are used as upstream intends, including from a composite (`SettingsFile.mount_into`).

options.name: Python-side builder with `build()`
options.note: It needs neither `Lazy` nor patches (checked in a scratch environment), but anything added after `build()` is silently lost, and accumulating across charts needs a shared builder object, which is a registry. Passing the complete list to the constructor needs neither.

options.name: JSON-patch accumulation on a built binding
options.note: `Bucket.grant` appends raw dicts at `/spec/access/-` (`seaweedfs/s3.py:223-229`), and `_ClusterGrant` is a chart singleton found by construct id (`s3.py:109-119`). The owner accepts a patch only as a required hatch (#7967), and a `/-` append needs an existing list.

options.name: Synth-time rendering (`Lazy`, a `to_json` override, App resolvers)
options.note: `Lazy` raises a jsii `TypeError` in any typed slot (#8067) and works only in `any`-typed ones such as HelmRelease `values`. A `to_json` override edits wire JSON after the generated mapping, and a resolver is app-global and would have to reach 10 `App(` sites.

design_space.pick: C1 and C3 build everything ducktape writes in one call, and cdk8s-plus's accumulators are used where upstream provides them (principle 3). The one amendment after construction is pod policy (C5).

design_space.question: How does a rule that applies to many objects, such as pod hardening or placement, get onto each of them?

options.name: Module constants and kwargs bundles
options.note: `WRITABLE_ROOT` (`container_security.py:10-12`) and the drop-ALL constants and TypedDict spread that #8115 and #8109 proposed each reach one pod dialect and hide which fields they set. Every author still has to remember to use them.

options.name: Defaults in wrapper constructors
options.note: Right for policy over one kind, stated in the function's docstring (`flux_kustomization`, `cnpg.cluster`; C2). A constructor default cannot reach the 54 raw `k8s.Kube*` workloads or the pod specs inside `SandboxTemplate` and `ScaledJob`.

options.name: Mutator functions on a built construct
options.note: `pod_policy.harden` and `place` find the pod spec through one kind-to-path table and fill only what is unset, on cdk8s-plus, raw and CRD pods alike (checked in a scratch environment with the real `SandboxTemplate` binding). They raise on a kind without a pod template.

options.name: Constructs mixins (`with_()`)
options.note: The same eager walk as a mutator, plus jsii `IMixin` ceremony. It silently skips constructs it does not support, and a chart-level call applies to every workload in the chart.

options.name: Admission-time mutation (Kyverno)
options.note: Kyverno mutates Pods the generator does not author and guards admission (`kyverno/policies.py:152-346`). Used as the default for generated objects, it would make the snapshot and the fleet rules misstate what runs.

options.name: Validation only (fleet rules)
options.note: A pure rule over rendered objects catches what a mutator missed, such as a container added after `harden()`. The writer attaches it to every chart, where 12 of 191 charts opt in today (C6).

design_space.pick: C5 fills pod policy on every dialect and C6 checks the result on every chart; policy over one kind is a C2 default. Kyverno keeps the Pods the generator does not author.

design_space.axis: How facts cross objects and modules
design_space.question: When two objects or two modules must agree on a name, port, label set or Secret key, what carries the fact?

options.name: Repeated strings
options.note: Today's default: ntfy's port is written 6 times in one module (`ntfy.py:68` and five reuses), `external-creds-reader` 31 times, and `-app`/`-rw` names are derived by hand 12 times.

options.name: Module constants
options.note: The only sanctioned carrier today (`cluster/cdk8s/AGENTS.md:52-57`). One constant holds one string, so a Service's name, port and Pod labels become three constants that each consumer recombines.

options.name: Construct references within one chart
options.note: Where cdk8s-plus holds a relation by construction (`Service(selector=deployment)`, `Volume.from_config_map`), the construct is the reference. It works only where both objects are built in the same synth, so it never reaches a consumer in another Kustomization.

options.name: Identity-only references
options.note: A frozen dataclass of names, keys, ports and labels, declared once by the producer and projected into each dialect by methods (C4). It needs the one boundary change in `cluster/cdk8s/AGENTS.md:8-13` (decision 1).

options.name: A registry or 'provides' declarations
options.note: `cluster/cdk8s/AGENTS.md:8-13` and `cluster/cdk8s/TODO.md:40-41` forbid it. A lookup resolved at synth hides which module a fact came from.

options.name: An intermediate app model or IR (Score, Timoni)
options.note: It is the parallel deployment specification PLAN.md F forbids; the proposal built on it scored 4/10 on owner fit. Its per-namespace SeaweedFS Tenant cannot be built where one namespace's buckets belong to several Kustomizations.

design_space.pick: C4 references for anything that crosses a module or a Kustomization, construct references inside one chart, and constants only for facts that are the same everywhere.

design_space.question: When a relationship has two halves (client egress and server ingress, a Secret's source grant and its copy, a bucket and its identity), who builds each half?

options.name: Each side by hand
options.note: Today's network wiring: the client's URL and egress rule and the server's ingress rule are written separately from string constants, and `cilium.endpoint_labels` gets a string name at 30 of 38 sites.

options.name: Grant methods on a built resource (AWS CDK Grants)
options.note: Both halves need an accumulation point, which on typed Python bindings is a JSON patch or a chart singleton (`Bucket.grant`, `_ClusterGrant`).

options.name: A facade returning both halves
options.note: The caller has to take the pair apart. #8111's combinator was indexed with `[1]`, the owner objected, and a flag was added to avoid the index.

options.name: Connections (cdk8s-plus `PodConnections`)
options.note: `allow_to` and `allow_from` write both directions from one call, but they emit `networking.k8s.io` NetworkPolicy, and this cluster enforces CiliumNetworkPolicy.

options.name: Two projections of one reference
options.note: The producer exports a `ServiceRef`; the client builds `url` and `egress()`, and the server admits the client's `Pods` on `pod_port`, each in its own chart (C4). Nothing is re-spelled, and no call site needs both charts.

options.name: A roster that authorizes both sides
options.note: A `Credential` names a Secret and its consumer namespaces once; the source's chart renders the Role, RoleBindings and store from it, and `copy()` refuses an unapproved consumer at synth (C8, #7455).

options.name: A composite that owns both sides
options.note: Where one owner builds both halves, one construct builds them and exposes the results (`PrivateBucket`: bucket, identity, credentials and grant; C3).

design_space.pick: C4 projections for network paths, the C8 roster for cross-namespace Secrets, and a C3 composite when one owner builds both halves.

design_space.axis: Output: the writer and the Flux node
design_space.question: Who writes a generated directory, and how does its Flux node learn what the directory contains?

options.name: A node that writes its own directory
options.note: No node function takes `root` today: the entry point writes each directory, with `write_directory` or a module's `write_manifests`, before calling its node (`generate_manifests.py:744-752`). `cluster/cdk8s/AGENTS.md:107-108` says a node writes no file, and `AGENTS.md:140-141` that a Kustomization never builds the chart it describes.

options.name: Facts passed to each node as keywords
options.note: Today's join: `SOPS_DECRYPTION` passed by hand at 26 nodes, 39 health-check entries typed out, and 22 of 40 stateful units without `deletionPolicy: Orphan`.

options.name: A writer that returns what it rendered
options.note: `write_directory` synthesizes the charts, writes `kustomization.yaml`, and returns a `RenderedDirectory` from which the node derives source, path and decryption (`generation.py:66-95`, landed in #8197). C7 extends it to attach the fleet rules and to derive Orphan.

options.name: A node base class or registry (#7444)
options.note: `cluster/cdk8s/AGENTS.md:127-130` and PLAN.md F forbid it, and a plain value returned by the writer gives the same derivation.

options.name: Hand-written kustomization glue
options.note: Only what must stay YAML: image-pins Components with their Setters markers, and SOPS siblings, both listed by the writer (P18).

design_space.pick: C7: one `write_directory` call per component returns a `RenderedDirectory`, and the node reads it. Nodes never write.

design_space.question: How many Kustomizations does a component get, what may a `dependsOn` edge express, and where does `wait` go?

options.name: A unit per concern (namespace, database, secrets, bucket, provisioner)
options.note: It produced the tiny units: 59 of 165 measurable Kustomizations render 3 objects or fewer, and each costs its own reconcile loop and I/O.

options.name: One Kustomization per component (#7094 rule 3)
options.note: A second unit only for CRDs or an operator, state not yet protected by Orphan, another source or age key, independent suspend, or another cadence. Derived Orphan (C7) makes folding stateful objects into the component safe.

options.name: Readiness edges
options.note: 35 of 249 edges wait on runtime state, 27 of them on a namespace unit (62 if the 27 direct `kyverno` edges count as runtime, as decision 13 recommends). Each turns a fault that heals by retry into a gate that propagates, with one alert per downstream node (#7094).

options.name: Admission-only edges (#7094 rule 1)
options.note: An edge points at the provider of a rendered kind's CRD, an operator whose `failurePolicy: Fail` webhook gates it, or a `postBuild.substituteFrom` source; 214 of today's 249 edges qualify, 27 of them direct `kyverno` edges that decision 13 would reclassify as runtime. Any other edge is an `ORDERING_EXCEPTIONS` entry with one of two reasons.

options.name: `dependsOn` derived from rendered kinds
options.note: Choosing the predecessor from a kind makes the graph implicit and turns the kind-to-provider map into the 'provides' registry the boundaries forbid. `OPERATOR_CRDS` stays a map that checks hand-passed edges.

options.name: Hand-passed edges checked at synth
options.note: Predecessors stay parameters (`cluster/cdk8s/AGENTS.md:107-130`), and validations on the kustomizations chart check CRD reachability and edge justification, which also closes the `parse_cluster` gap #7763 reported.

options.name: `wait` on every node
options.note: `wait` is true on 123 nodes, and 94 of them are unsuspended and gate nothing admission needs; each parks a kustomize-controller worker for `timeout` on every reconcile of a sick unit. The default becomes `None`, and only the 23 admission targets gate.

design_space.pick: C7 nodes with admission-only predecessors and `wait` only on admission targets, checked at synth by C6-style rules. #7094 is the governing policy (decision 2).

design_space.question: How does a program's configuration get from the generator into its Pod or its Terraform run?

options.name: Hand-spelled env names and config files
options.note: A renamed setting fails at runtime. The ConfigMap key, mount directory and `CONFIG_FILE_ENV` path are spelled separately today (`agentplane/actions.py:159-165, 189, 269-271`).

options.name: The binary's own pydantic `Settings`
options.note: `util/settings_contract` renders files, flags and env from the model, so a renamed field fails at synth, and secrets arrive under the field's env name (#7233, #7426). `SettingsFile` keeps key, mount and path in agreement (C9, C3).

options.name: A Terraform vars model checked against `variables.tf`
options.note: A frozen, `extra=forbid` model per module, tied to `variables.tf` by a relation test on top-level names, because tofu only warns on an undeclared variable (C9). Landed in #8152: `DnsRecordsVars`, `KeysVars` and `test_terraform_vars.py`.

options.name: Generating `variables.tf` from the model
options.note: It moves ownership of the module interface into the generator, and the relation test already catches the drift.

options.name: Typed Helm values
options.note: No chart here ships a values schema, so values stay dicts. Typed `k8s` structs go inside them where they carry placement or a Secret reference, and they render wire-shaped there (checked in a scratch environment).

options.name: A vendor binary's own mechanism
options.note: ntfy's `NTFY_*` env is built from one dict; an upstream tool's own config mechanism wins where it has one (#7461).

design_space.pick: C9: in-repo binaries render from their Settings, Terraform modules from a vars model under a relation test, and vendor binaries from their own mechanism built from one dict.

design_space.question: Which package owns a shape, and what may it import?

options.name: `providers/<crd>/`
options.note: CRD structure and its real variant shapes only, importing nothing from the `cluster/cdk8s` root (C1). The KEDA scaler shape that briefly lived there was a ducktape choice and moved out (#7952).

options.name: Policy modules at the package root
options.note: `flux.py`, `cnpg.py`, `gateway.py`, `pod_policy.py`, `node_scheduling.py` and `external_secrets/credentials.py`: one module per policy domain (C2, C5, C8).

options.name: Per-app modules
options.note: An app module owns its charts, its node and the references it exports (`ntfy.SERVICE`), so consumers import the producer (C3, C4, C7).

options.name: Constructs shipped by code packages
options.note: A `deploy/` package may ship a composite that imports only `providers/` and C4 references and takes every cluster fact as a parameter (`cluster/cdk8s/AGENTS.md:58-64`; N32).

options.name: A universal application base class or archetype
options.note: PLAN.md F and #7444 rule it out, and the intermediate-model proposal's `HttpService` archetype added default-deny policies nobody asked for at the call site.

design_space.pick: Schema in `providers/`, policy at the root, composition and references in the app module; a code package may ship a composite that takes its cluster facts as inputs.

design_space.question: Which overall design, scored out of 10 for feasibility / owner fit / maintainability in the judging step, do the conventions start from?

options.name: Construct-centric (AWS CDK L2/L3)
options.note: Scored 8 / 6 / 8 for single-shot kind classes, composites with typed outputs, pod-policy mixins and nodes reading a rendered directory. Its references, `RenderedDirectory` and single-shot relationships were taken, and its JSON-patch mixins and per-pair `SecretCopy` stores were left out.

options.name: Values-first (functional)
options.note: Scored 7 / 6 / 6 for declared references and a pure `PodPolicy.apply` over `k8s.PodSpec`. Its (group, kind) stateful keys and named hardening exemptions were taken; it would force the 20 fluent workloads onto raw bindings and cannot express a Pod that needs its token.

options.name: Intermediate model
options.note: Scored 6 / 4 / 6 for frozen need records with one renderer each and an `HttpService` archetype, the parallel specification PLAN.md F forbids. Its explicit token-mount decision, glue absorption into the writer and synth-time approval check were taken.

options.name: Consolidate existing mechanisms
options.note: Scored 8 / 7 / 8 for one existing mechanism per job, the AGENTS.md boundaries kept and the lowest migration risk. Its weak spots, cross-module agreement and opt-in enforcement, are covered by the grafted references and writer-attached rules.

design_space.pick: Consolidate is the base, with the construct-centric references and writer and the values-first stateful keys grafted in: C1-C9.

prior_art.name: Construct levels (L1, L2, L3)
prior_art.ecosystem: AWS CDK, the model for cdk8s and cdk8s-plus
prior_art.idea: Generated L1 classes, hand-written L2 classes with intent-based defaults and references, L3 patterns composing several resources, and an escape hatch to the raw resource.
prior_art.why: It is the layering vocabulary here: `providers/` kind classes are L1 wrappers (C1) and composites are L3 (C3). A Python L2 over a typed binding has to be single-shot, because TypeScript L2s render through `Lazy`.

prior_art.name: Grants (Facades)
prior_art.idea: `bucket.grants.read(role)` writes a permission on both the resource and the principal from one call.
prior_art.why: The one-call, two-sided idea survives as the `Credential` roster (C8), which declares both ends on the authorizing side. Grant methods that accumulate on a built resource need `Lazy` in typed slots, which Python cannot use.

prior_art.name: Connections
prior_art.idea: `a.connections.allowTo(b, port)` adds egress on one side and ingress on the other.
prior_art.why: cdk8s-plus's version emits stock NetworkPolicy, and this cluster uses CiliumNetworkPolicy. The idea is kept as two projections of one `ServiceRef` (`egress()` and `Pods.admit`), each built in its own side's chart (C4).

prior_art.name: Aspects
prior_art.idea: A deferred visitor over the whole construct tree during synthesis, which can mutate or validate.
prior_art.why: cdk8s 2.70 and constructs 10.8 have no Aspects. The validating half exists as `node.add_validation`, which the writer attaches to every chart (C6); a mutating visitor has no safe equivalent, because validations run 1+N times per synth.

prior_art.name: Mixins (`construct.with_()`)
prior_art.idea: An object with `supports()` and `applyTo()`, applied eagerly to a construct's subtree.
prior_art.why: It is the same eager walk as `harden()`, it silently skips unsupported constructs, and a chart-level call reaches every workload. The plain function raises instead (P10).

prior_art.name: Components with an Args class
prior_art.idea: `ComponentResource` subclasses built from a typed args object, with children parented to the component and outputs registered.
prior_art.why: It is the same shape as a C3 composite that takes typed inputs or an `Environment`. It confirms the shape and adds no mechanism.

prior_art.name: Transforms
prior_art.idea: Callbacks over each resource's type, name and props, applied to a component's children or stack-wide.
prior_art.why: They act at a distance over untyped prop bags. The cdk8s analogues, App resolvers and `to_json` overrides, are rejected for the same reason (P11).

prior_art.name: Object-merge mixins (`withX`, `withXMixin`)
prior_art.idea: Constructor functions return plain objects, and modifiers are partial objects merged with `+`.
prior_art.why: Untyped merges hide typos and ordering. jsii structs have no copy-with-changes, so the Python form would be partial dicts, against the typed-structs rule (`cluster/cdk8s/AGENTS.md:315-318`).

prior_art.name: Components
prior_art.idea: Opt-in bundles of resources, generators and patches applied at `kustomize build` time.
prior_art.why: Kept only where YAML is required: the image-pins Component carrying Setters markers for Flux image automation (P18). It is not a composition mechanism for generator code.

prior_art.name: Library charts
prior_art.idea: Shared named templates included by other charts, with ad hoc merge helpers.
prior_art.why: Text templating over YAML with no types; errors show up at render or apply time.

prior_art.name: Unification
prior_art.idea: Schemas, constraints and values unify, and a conflicting concrete value is an error.
prior_art.why: It is a new language and evaluator. Its useful idea, that a contradiction is an error, is what `place()` raising on a second placement and the fleet rules already provide.

prior_art.name: Workload spec with abstract resources
prior_art.idea: A workload declares typed resource needs (postgres, s3, dns, route), and a platform implementation provisions each and fills placeholders.
prior_art.why: It is an intermediate vocabulary plus a provisioner registry, which `cluster/cdk8s/AGENTS.md:8-13` forbids. The typed equivalent is a composite that builds real objects and exports references (C3, C4).

prior_art.name: Inventory classes
prior_art.idea: Hierarchical parameter classes deep-merged per target, then interpolated into templates.
prior_art.why: Which class won a value is invisible at the use site. The frozen `Environment` is the typed, explicit form of the useful part.

prior_art.name: Composition functions
prior_art.idea: A composite API served in the cluster by a pipeline of functions over desired state.
prior_art.why: It moves composition into the cluster, away from the committed, snapshot-tested output, and debugging moves from synth to the live cluster.

prior_art.name: Module system
prior_art.idea: Typed options merged by type, with explicit priorities (`mkDefault`, `mkForce`) deciding conflicts.
prior_art.why: It needs a lazy fixpoint evaluator and a global option namespace. Its priority idea is what `cluster/cdk8s/AGENTS.md:147-152` already says: a default is policy, and a node overrides it by keyword.

prior_art.name: cdk8s-plus itself
prior_art.idea: Hand-written L2s over a `Lazy`-rendered L1, with fluent mutators, construct references and `from_*_name` imports.
prior_art.why: Consumed as tier 1 for core kinds, with its accumulators used as upstream intends. Its authoring technique needs `Lazy` in typed props, which Python cannot do, so ducktape's own wrappers are single-shot.

prior_art.name: Plain functional builders
prior_art.ecosystem: Python; today's Flux graph and `Environment` pattern
prior_art.idea: Functions and classes take frozen props and already-built constructs and return constructs; a hand-ordered entry point passes results forward.
prior_art.why: It is the spine the conventions keep: every dependency is in a signature, and a wrong order is a `NameError` at synth (`cluster/cdk8s/AGENTS.md:107-130`).

principles.name: One shape per job
principles.statement: Each job the layer does has exactly one mechanism, chosen from mechanisms the tree already uses. A second shape for the same job is a review finding.
principles.why: Root causes 1 and 8: 199 shared helpers use 39 mechanism combinations, and each dedup PR proposed one more; #8113 and #8114 landed theirs. The rule landed in `cluster/cdk8s/AGENTS.md:82-86` (#8167). Choosing among shapes the tree already has keeps the learning cost and the migration diff small.

principles.name: Generated bindings are the model
principles.statement: Objects are built from cdk8s-plus, `k8s.Kube*` or `cdk8s_import` bindings. Ducktape code adds policy and wiring on top and never adds a parallel deployment specification or IR.
principles.why: The owner's first cdk8s review steered a hand-rolled spec record toward generated bindings (#7109), and PLAN.md F forbids a parallel deployment specification (`cluster/cdk8s/PLAN.md:124-125`).

principles.name: Build complete, once
principles.statement: Ducktape code builds each object from complete inputs in one constructor call and does not amend it afterwards. The one exception is `pod_policy.harden`/`place`. cdk8s-plus's own accumulators are used the way upstream intends.
principles.why: A `Lazy` in a typed Python slot raises a jsii `TypeError` (#8067). jsii structs are copied by value at construction, so later edits to them never reach the output. JSON-patch accumulation is the shape the owner accepts only as a required hatch (#7967). The rule, without the `pod_policy` exception, landed in `cluster/skills/cdk8s_builders/SKILL.md:21` (#8167).

principles.name: Facts cross as references
principles.statement: A fact that two objects or modules must agree on is declared once, by its producer, as an identity-only reference. Each consumer projects its own half from the reference and never spells it again.
principles.why: Root cause 3. It also meets the owner's 'no hand-copied strings the generated types already know' (#7969).

principles.name: Derive, do not restate
principles.statement: Anything computable from what was built is derived in the one place that knows it: decryption, `deletionPolicy: Orphan`, health checks, store allowlists, RoleBinding names, kustomization file lists.
principles.why: Root causes 5 and 7. The 22 missing Orphans and the store-allowlist outages both came from restated facts.

principles.name: Enforce by construction, then by rule
principles.statement: An invariant holds by construction where it can. Where it cannot, a pure synth-time rule checks every chart the writer produces and the whole Flux graph. Nothing relies on an author opting in.
principles.why: Fleet rules run on 12 of 191 charts today, and the graph check, which reads `kustomize build` output, cannot see the 11 CRD edges known only from their comments. Opt-in enforcement fails at the rate the inventory measured.

principles.name: providers/ is schema, the ducktape layer is policy
principles.statement: `providers/` holds CRD structure and its real variant shapes. Every namespace, name, zone, image or retention choice lives in a ducktape module.
principles.why: The owner's layering rule (#5099), confirmed by the KEDA incident (#7952) and written down at `cluster/cdk8s/AGENTS.md:344-354`.

principles.name: Admission, not readiness
principles.statement:
A Flux `dependsOn` edge exists only where the API server would reject the dependent's objects without the target: the provider of a rendered kind's CRD, the operator whose `failurePolicy: Fail` webhook gates it, or a `postBuild.substituteFrom` source. Everything else converges by retry.
`wait` and health checks sit only on a node such an edge points at, and a component is one Kustomization.
principles.why: Readiness edges turn a fault that heals by retry into a gate that propagates, and the tiny units they produced cost reconcile time and I/O, which is the owner's reason for the change (#7094). On devel aaaa3a5b90, 35 of 249 edges are not admission edges (62 if the 27 direct `kyverno` edges count as runtime, as decision 13 recommends), 94 of the 123 `wait: true` nodes are unsuspended and gate nothing admission needs, and 59 of 165 measurable units render 3 objects or fewer.

diagnosis:
No target shape per job, so each helper author chose one. 199 shared helpers use 39 mechanism combinations. `providers/` is uniform apart from seaweedfs: its `Identity` and `Bucket` are plain Constructs taking `name=, namespace=` (`providers/seaweedfs/s3.py:59-73,89-108`), while the other 21 kind constructors take `metadata=`. The layer above it is not:
- six policy functions that each build and return one object take its identity six ways: `cnpg.cluster(scope, id, *, name=, namespace=)` (`cnpg.py:58-63`), `gitops_terraform(scope, id, *, name=)` (`terraform.py:51-55`), `https_route(scope, id, *, metadata=)` (`gateway.py:51-55`), `helm_release(scope, name, namespace)` with a derived id (`helm.py:36-39,73`), `valkey_instance(scope, *, name=, namespace=)` with `name` as the id (`valkey.py:74-78,95`), and `flux_kustomization(chart, name, source)` (`flux.py:132-135`);
- reading a Secret key into env has the shared `env_helpers` pair (`env_helpers.py:8-17`, 50 calls) and 11 module-local copies, 10 raw and one fluent (for example `haku_egress_proxy.py:57`, `ntfy.py:78`).
'One shape per job' (`cluster/cdk8s/AGENTS.md:82-86`) asks for one mechanism per job but points at whatever the tree already does, and 'One helper per repeated shape' (`:87-94`) names shapes, not mechanisms; its own examples mix a mutator (`node_scheduling.py`), a JSON patch (`pod_spec_patches.py`) and value factories.

The TypeScript cdk8s-plus idiom, where an L2 accumulates state and renders its L1 through `Lazy`, cannot be reproduced on typed Python bindings: a `Lazy` in a typed slot raises a jsii typeguard `TypeError`, as #8067 recorded. Helpers that wanted incremental APIs emulated it:
- `Bucket.grant` appends a raw dict at `/spec/access/-` (`cluster/cdk8s/seaweedfs/s3.py:223-229`);
- `_grant_cluster_reference` finds a `_ClusterGrant` chart singleton by construct id (`seaweedfs/s3.py:109-119`).
The owner accepts a JSON patch only as a required hatch (#7967).

Writers come in three shapes. `generation.write_directory` (`generation.py:66-95`) writes 100 directories and returns the `flux.RenderedDirectory` its node reads, so no node function takes `root`, as `cluster/cdk8s/AGENTS.md:140-141` requires. The rest come from 63 module-writer calls at `generate_manifests.py:256-336`, through `write_charts` or a module's own `App` (6 modules); they list their files in a hand-written `kustomization.yaml`, write their own (20 `write_yaml` sites, for example `tofu_state/db.py:87-97`) or leave Flux to generate one, and hold 22 `<id>.k8s.yaml` literals. Adding a directory touches three places in `generate_manifests.py`, four when it keeps a module writer.

The dedup PRs treat symptoms, because there was no target to dedupe toward. The two that landed each add another shape for a job that already has one:
- composites that return `None`, against the skill's rule that a helper returns what it builds (`cluster/skills/cdk8s_builders/SKILL.md:31`): `mint_bearer_secret` with 12+ knobs and `mint_db_role_secret` (#8114, `external_secrets/minted_secret.py:37-54, 96-110`);
- thin constructor wrappers (#8113, `env_helpers.py:8-17`).
#8111's combinator grew an `include_dns` flag after the owner objected to callers indexing its result.

needs_intro: Every row below is a job the generator does today or will need to do as more of the cluster becomes code. They come from the repo's plans and TODOs, the remainder backlog, open issues, the Flux dependency work, and what the modules repeat. The frequency tag says how often each comes up.

patterns.name: Constant
patterns.reason: Allowed for facts that are the same everywhere: `Placement` values, `BEARER_PASSWORD`, `POSTGRES_IMAGE` and other `# renovate:` pins, exported references, a directory's `SIBLINGS` tuple, and the checking tables `OPERATOR_CRDS` and `flux.ORDERING_EXCEPTIONS`. Not allowed for per-app configuration (#4678) or for bundles of policy structs (`WRITABLE_ROOT`, #8115's drop-ALL pair, `SOPS_DECRYPTION` passed at call sites). Those become `harden()`, C2 defaults, or derivations.

patterns.name: Value factory
patterns.reason: Only a function that derives something (`cilium.fqdn_fence`, `RenderedDirectory.health_checks`, `PostgresRef.rw`, `cnpg.same_owner_initdb` deriving the owner role from the database name) and returns a generated struct or a plain value. A function that only forwards its arguments to one constructor is not written (#7461: `_secret_env`; #8168 deleted `metadata()` on this rule); that covers the merged `env_helpers` (#8113). No factory returns a kwargs TypedDict to spread (`LONG_LIVED_CA`, `cert_manager/cluster_ca.py:35-41`).

patterns.name: Classmethod factories
patterns.reason: The single shape for schema variants: `@staticmethod`s on a concept-named class that return the generated struct (`EgressRule.to_entities` #7969, `Rule.alert` #8010, `Endpoint.bearer_authorization` #8098). No `providers/` factory returns a wrapper to unwrap: C1 converted the `.to_spec()` wrappers (#8148, #8150, #8151, #8158, #8164), and the builder skill states the shape (`cluster/skills/cdk8s_builders/SKILL.md:61`). Classmethods on our own frozen values (`PostgresRef.generated`) follow the same shape.

patterns.name: Kind wrapper class
patterns.reason: Already the majority shape in `providers/`. A subclass of the binding stays an `ApiObject` that `ApiObject.of`, `harden()` and `RenderedDirectory` can see. It is single-shot, takes `metadata: ApiObjectMetadata`, and holds no ducktape facts.

patterns.name: Composite construct
patterns.reason: The one shape for a repeated group of two or more objects. Its objects and references are attributes, so nothing returns `None` or a name, as #8114's `mint_bearer_secret` and `mint_db_role_secret` do today, and it renders in its owner's Kustomization. Limited by 'two call sites, no application base class' (PLAN.md F, #7444).

patterns.name: Resource function
patterns.reason: Ducktape policy over one kind (`flux_kustomization` with 172 calls, `cnpg.cluster`, `https_route`, `helm_release`, `gitops_terraform`), plus `credentials.grant`/`copy` and `write_directory`. About 280 call sites already use it, and converting them to classes buys nothing.

patterns.name: Mutator on a built construct
patterns.reason: Exactly two: `pod_policy.harden` and `pod_policy.place`. Pod policy is the one concern that must reach cdk8s-plus, raw and CRD pod specs, and an explicit function that raises on a kind without a pod template reaches all three; this was checked in a scratch environment on a cdk8s-plus Deployment, a raw CronJob and the real `SandboxTemplate` binding. `attract_to_zone`, `tolerate_control_plane_taint` and `apply_pod_spec_patches` are deleted.

patterns.name: Incremental methods
patterns.reason:
cdk8s-plus's own accumulators are used as upstream intends: `add_container`, `mount`, `env.add_variable`, `Role.allow`, `add_subjects`, and `SettingsFile.mount_into`, which calls them. Ducktape classes do not add accumulating methods.
On a built typed binding, accumulation means JSON-patch appends or a singleton lookup (`Bucket.grant`, `_ClusterGrant`). A Python-side builder that constructs once in `build()` avoids both, as a scratch-environment check showed, but it adds a finalize step and silently drops anything added after `build()`. A complete list passed to the constructor (C1 `access=`, C8 `consumers=`) states the same thing without an ordering rule.

patterns.name: JSON patch
patterns.reason: Only inside `pod_policy` (fill-if-absent, typed `k8s` struct values) and for a field a typed tier-1 constructor lacks (`topologySpreadConstraints`). Checked sharp edges: a `/-` append needs an existing list, a patch under an absent parent throws at synth, and a path outside the binding's schema is silently dropped. All three are too sharp for call sites.

patterns.name: Constructs mixin
patterns.reason: `with_()` is the same eager subtree walk as `harden()`. It adds jsii `IMixin` ceremony (a frozen dataclass cannot implement it) and silently skips constructs it does not support, where the plain function raises. A chart-level `with_(Pinned(...))` would also pin every workload in the chart.

patterns.name: Synth-time rendering
patterns.reason:
In Python, `Lazy` works only in `any`-typed slots: `metadata.add`, HelmRelease `values`, a CRD schema example. In a typed field it raises (#8067). cdk8s-plus still uses `Lazy` internally, and the layer uses its accumulators. Even in `any`-typed Helm values, a `Lazy` would make the rendered values depend on call order across the chart function, visible only in the snapshot, for values that can be computed up front.
A `to_json` override edits wire JSON after the generated mapping, where no reader looks, and App resolvers are app-global. One checked fact is kept for later: a JSON patch of a core PodSpec into a CRD slot is filtered by the CRD's `toJson` whitelist, and a `to_json` override is not. No need in N1-N34 requires it.

patterns.name: Props / profile value
patterns.reason: The frozen `Environment` per namespace stays unchanged. `Placement`, `FleetExceptions`, `Credential` and the Settings and Terraform-vars models are the same kind of value: data only, never callables (`cluster/cdk8s/AGENTS.md:37-42`).

patterns.name: Typed outputs and references
patterns.reason: Identity-only references declared by producers (`SecretRef`, `SecretKey`, `Port`, `Pods`, `ServiceRef`, `PostgresRef`), composite attributes, and the writer's `RenderedDirectory`. This is the root-cause fix for re-spelled strings, and it needs the one boundary change.

patterns.name: Relationship facade
patterns.reason: Only the `Credential` roster, which declares both ends of a Secret read on the authorizing side, as the owner's external-creds standard does (#7455). A network relationship is two projections of one reference; a facade that returns a pair gets split by index (#8111). Per-pair stores built from the consumer's chart (`single_secret_store`, the proposed `SecretCopy`) are rejected.

patterns.name: Intermediate model
patterns.reason: It is the parallel deployment specification PLAN.md F forbids, and it invites field creep. Its per-namespace SeaweedFS Tenant cannot be built where one namespace's buckets belong to several Kustomizations: namespace monitoring holds separate grants for mimir and tempo. Pydantic models that mirror a consumer's own schema (Settings, `variables.tf`) are C9, and `RenderedDirectory` records what was built; neither describes what to build.

patterns.name: Validation
patterns.reason: Pure rules over rendered objects, attached by the writer to every chart, with exceptions as `FleetExceptions` fields. The same mechanism checks the Flux graph on the kustomizations chart: CRD reachability, edge justification against `flux.ORDERING_EXCEPTIONS`, and gating only on admission targets. The hardening rule shares `POD_SPEC_PATHS` with `harden()`, so the check and the fix agree.

patterns.name: Admission-time mutation
patterns.reason: Kyverno handles Pods the generator does not author (Helm charts, operators, agents) and serves as admission defence. It is never the source of a default for a generated object, because the snapshot and the fleet rules cannot see it.

patterns.name: Kustomize-side composition
patterns.reason: Allowed for hand-written image-pins Components (Setters markers must be YAML), SOPS siblings and configMapGenerator entries, all listed by `write_directory`. No Kustomize patches or replacements over generated objects (#5068), and no `postBuild` substitution of a value the generator knows: `LETSENCRYPT_ISSUER` renders in Python (#8160).

patterns_intro: The design-space axes above are built from these pattern families: every shape a helper in this layer can take, from a constant to an intermediate model. Each gets a verdict: adopt it as a convention, restrict it to named cases, or reject it. The matrix below scores each family against each need.
mechanics: `Lazy` works only in `any`-typed slots, such as `metadata.add(...)` or HelmRelease `values`. Put into a typed struct field, it fails jsii's type check with a `TypeError`, which is why #8067 was closed. The TypeScript cdk8s-plus pattern, where a wrapper renders its spec lazily from mutable state, cannot be reproduced on typed Python bindings.
Generated structs (`k8s.*`, CRD `*Spec` types, cdk8s-plus props) are read-only values copied into the construct at construction. Mutating one afterwards changes nothing.

cdk8s-plus classes are real accumulators: `add_container`, `mount`, `env.add_variable`, `Role.allow`, `add_subjects` and metadata labels all show up at synth when called later. Fields captured from props at construction (a container's `securityContext`, image, resources, probes) can only change through a JSON patch.

There are no Aspects in cdk8s 2.70 or constructs 10.8. The constructs `IMixin` and `construct.with_(...)` work from Python, but they are eager: they apply to the subtree as it exists at call time and silently skip constructs they don't support.
`node.add_validation` runs 1+N times per synth (N charts), so a validation must be pure. `App(resolvers=[...])` works from Python but is app-global.
Overriding `to_json()` in a Python subclass of a generated binding works: cdk8s calls it at synth. It edits wire-shaped JSON after all other rendering.
JSON patches on typed bindings apply before the generated field mapping, so paths use the binding's property names and values should be typed structs.
cdk8s-plus's `ServiceAccount` renders `automountServiceAccountToken: false` by default, so converting a raw ServiceAccount silently removes the token from pods that relied on it.

conventions.rule:

It subclasses the `cdk8s_import` binding and is constructed once as `Kind(scope, id, *, metadata: ApiObjectMetadata, <spec fields as same-named keywords>)`; `None` leaves a field to the operator's default.
It holds no ducktape fact (namespace, zone, cluster name) and has no method that changes it after construction: a list such as bucket access is passed whole.
A nested value whose schema has real variants gets a class named after the schema concept, whose `@staticmethod`s return the generated struct itself, so a hand-built struct is always accepted in its place.

conventions.name: Composite construct for a repeated group of objects
conventions.rule:
A shape that builds two or more objects and repeats at two or more call sites is a `Construct` subclass. It builds all its objects in `__init__` from typed inputs, and its public attributes are the objects it built and the C4 references consumers need (`access_key`, `generator`, `object_store`); it never returns `None` or a name for the caller to rebuild. Its policy is stated in its docstring, and a keyword appears only when a second caller needs it. A composite may call cdk8s-plus's own accumulators on objects it is handed (`SettingsFile.mount_into` calls `container.mount` and `container.env.add_variable`).
A composite renders in the owning component's Kustomization, never in a unit of its own (#7094 rule 3).
- `PrivateBucket` derives its credential Secret as `<name>-s3-credentials`, the spelling attic, forgejo and registry-cache already use, and takes the live name where a consumer spells it otherwise: renaming `secretRef` in place makes the operator mint a new key pair (decision 10). `local_identity: bool` places the S3Identity in the tenant or in the SeaweedFS namespace, and the grant is built under an `if` and is not an attribute.
- `PostgresBackup` lives in `cnpg_backup.py`, which imports `cnpg` and `seaweedfs.s3`; in `cnpg.py` it would close the Bazel cycle `cnpg -> seaweedfs:s3 -> seaweedfs:cluster -> seaweedfs:filer_db -> cnpg`.
- A reference is named after its concept; where a module already uses the name for a string (`authentik/db.py`'s `DATABASE = "authentik"`), the reference is `POSTGRES`.
conventions.when_to_use: `MintedSecret` (the 14 `mint_bearer_secret` and `mint_db_role_secret` calls, and Agentplane Dex's own generator pairs), `PrivateBucket` (bucket, identity, credentials, grant), `PostgresBackup`, `ResticBackup` (the copied VolSync modules), `SettingsFile`, and each app's top-level Construct (`Ntfy`, the agentplane constructs that take the `Environment`).
conventions.when_not: One object with policy: use C2. A group built once: write the kinds inline. A universal application base class or archetype (PLAN.md F, #7444). A knob kept only to reproduce one caller's output byte for byte (#8114); keeping a live Secret's name is a different matter, because renaming it destroys a credential.

conventions.name: Pod-template policy is two functions over one path table
conventions.rule:
Cluster pod policy is `pod_policy.harden(workload)` and `pod_policy.place(workload, placement, *, tolerate_control_plane=False)`. Each is called once on a finished workload of any dialect: cdk8s-plus, `k8s.Kube*`, or a CRD that embeds a pod template. Each finds the pod spec through `ApiObject.of` and `POD_SPEC_PATHS`, the kind-to-path table the fleet rules also read, and patches in only what is absent, using typed `k8s` struct values, so a value set at construction wins.
- `harden` sets RuntimeDefault seccomp on the Pod, and no privilege escalation and drop-ALL capabilities on each init and main container.
- `place` sets the `Placement`'s nodeSelector, and with `tolerate_control_plane` adds `CONTROL_PLANE_TOLERATION` and `PREFER_WORKERS`, so the Pod uses control-plane nodes only when workers are full. It raises on a pod spec that is already placed.
- An unknown kind raises `KeyError`.
`node_scheduling.py` exports `Placement`, `CONTROL_PLANE_TOLERATION` (`k8s.Toleration`) and `PREFER_WORKERS` (`k8s.Affinity`). `cnpg.cluster`'s affinity takes the same `Placement`, and Helm values and operator CRs embed the same values directly: typed `k8s` structs render wire-shaped inside `any`-typed values, while quantities there stay strings.
Per-image facts (uid and gid, a writable root, added capabilities, `automountServiceAccountToken`) are stated at construction. Converting a `KubeServiceAccount` to a cdk8s-plus `ServiceAccount` turns its token off (`automount_token` defaults to `False`), so the same change states `automount_service_account_token` on every Pod that runs as that account: `True` where the Pod calls the API, as tana-mcp's firebase resigner does.
These are the only ducktape functions that write JSON patches, apart from a field a typed tier-1 constructor lacks.
conventions.when_to_use: Every Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Job, CronJob, SandboxTemplate and ScaledJob the generator writes.
conventions.when_not: Pods a Helm chart or an operator creates: their values or CR fields take the same typed placement values, and their hardening is the chart's own values plus Kyverno admission, outside `harden()` and the fleet rules. Anything that adds objects. Metadata labels and annotations, which cdk8s-plus's metadata API or the constructor sets.
conventions.replaces:
- `apply_pod_spec_patches` and `runtime_default_seccomp_patch` (`pod_spec_patches.py`; its dead `CRON_JOB_POD_SPEC_PATH` already went in #8099).
- `attract_to_zone` and `tolerate_control_plane_taint` (`node_scheduling.py:10-20`).
- `WRITABLE_ROOT` (`container_security.py:10-12`): its 11 sites keep only `read_only_root_filesystem=False`.
- The literal hardening structs on raw and CRD pods (`attic.py:106-113, 266-279`; `agent_workspaces.py:91-113`).
- 14 local zone constants, 26 hand-written `nodeSelector` dicts in Helm values and ClickHouse pod templates, and about 15 hand-written prefer-workers affinities (`gatus/app.py:117-134`, `grocy/mcp.py:87`, ...).
conventions.why:
Pod policy is the one concern that must reach three pod dialects. In a scratch environment, `harden()` and `place()` ran on a cdk8s-plus Deployment, a raw `KubeCronJob` with an initContainer, and the real `SandboxTemplate` binding; all three rendered Pod seccomp, per-container drop-ALL, no escalation, the nodeSelector and the toleration. An explicit `NET_ADMIN` add and `readOnlyRootFilesystem: false` survived, and a second `place()` raised. The two Agentplane services that tolerate the control plane do so 'to schedule there under pressure' (`node_scheduling.py:1-4`), which is what `PREFER_WORKERS` states.
Fill-if-absent is chosen over raise-if-set because cdk8s-plus always renders a container securityContext, so raise-if-set would force every fluent workload onto raw bindings. The exemptions stay named anyway, because the fleet rule requires the result and lists exemptions at the writer.

conventions.name: Fleet rules run on every chart, attached by the writer

`generation.write_charts`, which `write_directory` calls for its charts (`generation.py:88`), registers `FleetRules` on every chart it synthesizes, so a directory that keeps a hand-written `kustomization.yaml` gets the rules too. Chart functions no longer call `add_fleet_rules`: the PR that attaches the rules at the writer for a chart deletes that chart's own call, since keeping both reports every finding twice.
A rule is a pure function `objects -> list[str]` over rendered dicts; validations run 1+N times per synth, so a rule never mutates. Exceptions are fields of a `FleetExceptions` value passed at the writer call, never names matched inside a rule. The hardening rule walks `pod_policy.POD_SPEC_PATHS`, so the check and the fix cannot disagree about where a pod spec lives. A relation that holds by construction (C3, C4) gets no rule.
The Flux graph is checked the same way: pure rules on the kustomizations chart check CRD reachability, edge justification and gating (C7 shows their shape), and their exception table is `flux.ORDERING_EXCEPTIONS`, whose entries carry a reason.

conventions.rule:
`write_directory(root, artifact, *chart_builders, siblings=(), namespace=None, components=(), config_map_generator=())` synthesizes a component's charts, writes `kustomization.yaml` listing them, the hand-written siblings, the components and the configMapGenerator entries, and returns a frozen `RenderedDirectory` holding the artifact and the decryption a SOPS sibling calls for (#8192; `generation.py:66-95`). The convention adds `chart_kinds=()` and `fleet=FleetExceptions()`: the writer attaches the fleet rules (C6), and `RenderedDirectory` also carries the identities of the rendered objects and the custom-resource kinds a HelmRelease there renders (`chart_kinds`), which the objects cannot show.
`ObjectId`, `STATEFUL_KINDS` and `api_objects(chart)`, which walks `chart.node.find_all()` because `Chart.api_objects` sees direct children only, join `RenderedDirectory` and `artifact_directory(artifact)` in `flux.py`, their only dispatcher, so the import stays `generation -> flux`.
- One component is one `write_directory` call and one node (#7094 rule 3). It gets a second unit only for CRDs or an operator, state not yet protected by a derived Orphan, another source or age key, independent suspend, or another cadence.
- A node for a generated directory is `name(chart, directory: RenderedDirectory, *predecessors) -> Kustomization` (`cluster/cdk8s/AGENTS.md:107-126`). `flux_kustomization` derives `sourceRef`, `path` and decryption, raising on an explicit `path=` or `decryption=` (`flux.py:174-190`), and adds `deletionPolicy: Orphan` whenever the directory renders a stateful (API group, kind). `deletion_policy=None` means derive, so a disposable cache passes `MIRROR_PRUNE` or `DELETE`, and a directory whose state lives inside a chart (a HelmRelease with persistence: loki, mimir, matrix) passes `ORPHAN`.
- A predecessor is an admission prerequisite of something the directory renders: the provider of its CRD; the operator whose `failurePolicy: Fail` webhook gates it (ESO, CNPG, cert-manager, virt-api, CDI, and Kyverno only as decision 13 settles it; prometheus-operator, SeaweedFS, tofu-controller and Valkey have none, so their consumers need only the CRD); or a `postBuild.substituteFrom` source. Any other edge is an entry in `flux.ORDERING_EXCEPTIONS`, whose reason is that the bootstrap never converges without it or that applying out of order destroys something (#7094 rule 2).
- `wait` defaults to `None` (Flux: off). Only an admission target passes `wait=True`, or `health_check_exprs` where the object has no Ready condition (kubevirt, cdi; #7699); its health checks come from `directory.health_checks(kinds)`.
- Synth-time validations on the kustomizations chart read each node's `RenderedDirectory` and fail when a rendered custom-resource kind does not reach its provider in `OPERATOR_CRDS`, when an edge is neither admission-justified nor listed, when `wait` or a health check sits on a node no such edge targets, or when an admission target does not gate. They check hand-passed edges; they never choose them.
- A value the generator knows renders in Python, never through `postBuild` substitution.
The entry point builds the artifact, calls the writer, then the node, and last hands every directory to the graph validation and every artifact to `write_artifact_generators`. Nodes never write.
conventions.when_to_use: Every directory the generator writes, including hand-written kustomization glue being absorbed (nix-cache's components and configMapGenerator; the owner asked for this in #7920). Every Flux node and every `dependsOn` edge.
conventions.when_not:
- Choosing `dependsOn` from rendered kinds: the map checks edges and never picks them, so the graph stays readable in the entry point.
- Ordering updates between two units: an edge orders the bootstrap only, since a dependent sourced from another artifact sees its prerequisite Ready at the old revision; updates that must be ordered share one artifact (#7094 rule 6).
- A hand-written directory passes its artifact, and a GitRepository node its sourceRef and path; the whole-tree test covers their edges until they convert.
- A CNPG Cluster whose `initdb.secret` ESO mints must not exist before that Secret (`cluster/docs/cnpg_conventions.md` R4), so it keeps an ordered unit with an `ORDERING_EXCEPTIONS` entry (destructive if out of order), or reads CNPG's generated `<name>-app` instead.

The 22 `.k8s.yaml` literals are in the directories a module's own `write_manifests` still writes (`forgejo/app.py:465`, `home_assistant/app.py:692`, ...).

conventions.why:
The rendered directory is exactly what the Kustomization reads at runtime (`cluster/cdk8s/AGENTS.md:142-146`) and a plain value testable by hand. Nodes already take it (`AGENTS.md:107-126`), so the join rule at `AGENTS.md:131-141` changes in one respect: health checks and Orphan cross inside that one value, where keywords computed at the join carry them today. Derivation makes the observed failures, a forgotten decryption or a forgotten Orphan, impossible; decryption already derives for every directory the writer writes (`generation.py:95`), and the same rendered objects are what the admission checks need.
Admission-only edges follow the owner's direction and #7094: a readiness edge turns a fault that heals by retry into a gate that propagates, and the tiny units it produced cost reconcile time and I/O. Derived Orphan covers the delete-or-rename case that #7094 rule 3b keeps a narrow unit for, which is what makes folding stateful objects into their component safe.
Checked in a scratch environment at c34eb113: the writer attaches the rules, lists the kustomization resources and sets the encrypted flag; (group, kind) detection counts a CNPG Cluster and a PVC and ignores `example.io/Cluster`; `Chart.api_objects` returns nothing for a Cluster nested in a construct, while `find_all` finds it. conventions.name: Secrets cross namespaces only through a Credential
conventions.rule:
A `Credential(source: SecretRef, consumers: frozenset[str])` is the only authorization for a Secret to be read outside its namespace, and `Credential.__post_init__` raises on an empty consumer set. SOPS sources are named constants in `external_creds.py`; an in-cluster source (a minted bearer, a controller output) is declared beside its producer.
- Source side: the chart that owns the source Secret calls `credentials.grant(chart, *credentials)` once, because that chart owns the namespace's one store. It renders an exact-name, get-only Role per Secret, a RoleBinding per consumer namespace's `external-creds-reader` named `<secret>-<namespace>-reader`, and the namespace's one referent-auth ClusterSecretStore `external-creds-<namespace>`, whose namespace list is derived from the consumers. It renders in the source's existing unit, never a new one.
- Consumer side: `credentials.copy(scope, id, credential=, target=SecretRef, keys=)` renders the ExternalSecret and fails synth when `target.namespace` is not approved. The consumer namespace's `external-creds-reader` ServiceAccount is created once, by the chart that creates that namespace (flux-system's by the external-creds chart).
- Flux: a consumer's only edge for a copy is `external-secrets-operator`, whose `failurePolicy: Fail` webhook admits the ExternalSecret; ESO retries until the store exists. The external-creds node depends on `external-secrets-operator`, because the ClusterSecretStore CRD and webhook must exist before its store applies.
New random values are C3 `MintedSecret`s.
conventions.when_to_use: Every cross-namespace Secret read: SOPS credentials, bearers minted on the server and copied to clients, pull credentials, controller-published tokens.
conventions.when_not: A Secret consumed only in its own namespace. Kubernetes-native identity and PKI (TokenRequest, cert-manager). Runtime brokers whose CRD is its own roster (Agentplane `EgressCredential`).
conventions.replaces:
- `single_secret_store` and its 10 per-pair stores built from the consumer's chart (`external_secrets/single_secret_store.py:20-74`; `agentplane/staging.py:379-398`), and its hand-rolled copy (`litellm/credentials.py:37-98`).
- ESO-ServiceAccount stores with hand-kept allowlists (`external_secrets/config.py:43-192`; forgejo-images lists 34 namespaces) and app-owned stores (`ntfy.py:82-112`).
- Reflector mirrors (`aiquota.py:191-211`) and ClusterExternalSecret used for copying.
- 17 copies of the reader ServiceAccount, including three owners of flux-system's, and hand-typed RoleBinding names (`external_creds.py:40-153`).
conventions.why: The owner asked for 'the standard pattern in external-creds' and no extra Kustomizations for credential plumbing (#7455, #7456). Five mechanisms become one, and the allowlist is derived from the roster. Exact-name Roles keep the property `ha_mcp.py:118-120` relies on: the Home Assistant admin token in the same namespace stays unreachable. Checked in a scratch environment against the committed output: `grant()` over the whole roster renders all 26 existing Roles and RoleBindings byte-identical, with one RoleBinding renamed; a roster entry with no consumers would have rendered a dangling Role, which `__post_init__` now refuses. Consumers' edges to stores and credential suppliers went in #8183, #8186 and #8188, finishing what #7559 began; the edge a copy keeps is to the operator whose webhook admits its ExternalSecret.

conventions.name: Configuration renders from the consumer's own model
conventions.rule:
Configuration a program reads is rendered from a model of that program's own schema:
- An in-repo binary: its pydantic Settings through `util/settings_contract`. `settings_file` goes into a `SettingsFile` ConfigMap (C3); `env_name` and `cli_args` render flags and env; secrets arrive as `SecretKey` projections under the Settings field's env name (#7426).
- A Terraform module: its variables are a frozen, `extra=forbid` pydantic model that mirrors `variables.tf`, passed as `gitops_terraform(variables=...)`, and one relation test ties each model's top-level field names to `variables.tf` (nested object attributes stay unchecked); the module's BUILD exports `variables.tf` for it. This landed in #8152 (`terraform.py:51-110`, `test_terraform_vars.py:20-25`). Terraform CRs group per external system (authentik-tf and github-tf, grouped in #8220 and #8222; forgejo-gitops) unless a #7094 rule-3 exception applies, and order among themselves through the CR's own `spec.dependsOn` (`gitops_terraform(depends_on=...)`), never through Flux `dependsOn`.
- A vendor binary keeps its own env or config mechanism, built from one dict (ntfy's `NTFY_*` env).
Reloader runs with `autoReloadAll` (`reloader.py:42`): a workload opts out with `"false"`, and no object carries `"true"` (#8108, #8157; `cluster/cdk8s/AGENTS.md:75-81`).
conventions.when_to_use: Every config file, flag list and env block of an in-repo service. Every tofu-controller Terraform CR.
conventions.when_not: Helm values, which stay untyped dicts in `helm_release` callers because no chart here ships a schema. An upstream tool's own config mechanism, which is preferred when it exists (#7461).

# terraform.py: the signature and the vars rendering landed in #8152
def gitops_terraform(
    scope: Construct,
    id: str,
    *,
    name: str,
    variables: BaseModel | None,
    depends_on: Sequence[TerraformV1Alpha2] = (),
    env: Sequence[TerraformV1Alpha2SpecRunnerPodTemplateSpecEnv] = (),
    env_from: Sequence[TerraformV1Alpha2SpecRunnerPodTemplateSpecEnvFrom] = (),
    schema: str | None = None,
    store_readable_plan: TerraformV1Alpha2SpecStoreReadablePlan | None = None,
) -> TerraformV1Alpha2:
    """... `variables` models the module's variables.tf (None: it declares none); each field is written
    structurally into the runner's tfvars. `depends_on` orders this CR after other Terraform CRs of the
    same external system, in the same unit, through the CR's own spec.dependsOn."""
    ...
            vars=None
            if variables is None
            else [TerraformV1Alpha2SpecVars(name=key, value=value) for key, value in variables.model_dump(mode="json").items()],
            depends_on=[TerraformV1Alpha2SpecDependsOn(name=dependency.name) for dependency in depends_on] or None,

- The six one-CR Forgejo module units (`forgejo/gitops_modules.py:50-69`), which group into `forgejo-gitops`. The typed `variables` and `depends_on` (#8152) and the authentik-tf and github-tf groups (#8220, #8222) have landed.

class PrivateBucket(Construct):
    """Bucket `name` in `tenant`, read-write for the one S3Identity of the same name (in `tenant` when
    `local_identity`, else in the SeaweedFS namespace). The operator writes that identity's key pair into
    Secret `<name>-s3-credentials`, or `secret_name` where a live consumer already reads another name.
    A grant admits exactly the kinds this puts outside the SeaweedFS namespace. Everything Retains."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        scope: Construct,
        id: str,
        *,
        name: str,
        tenant: str,
        local_identity: bool,
        adopt_existing: bool,
        description: str,
        secret_name: str | None = None,  # None: `<name>-s3-credentials`
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(scope, id)
        described = {"description": description}
        identity_namespace = tenant if local_identity else seaweedfs_namespace.NAME
        secret = SecretRef(namespace=tenant, name=secret_name or f"{name}-s3-credentials")
        self.bucket = Bucket(
            self,
            "bucket",
            metadata=ApiObjectMetadata(name=name, namespace=tenant, annotations=described),
            cluster_ref=BucketSpecClusterRef(name=cluster.NAME, namespace=seaweedfs_namespace.NAME),
            access=[BucketAccess.read_write(name)],
            adopt_existing=adopt_existing,
            reclaim_policy=BucketSpecReclaimPolicy.RETAIN,
        )
        self.identity = S3Identity(
            self,
            "identity",
            metadata=ApiObjectMetadata(name=name, namespace=identity_namespace, annotations=described),
            seaweed_ref=S3IdentitySpecSeaweedRef(name=cluster.NAME, namespace=_seaweed_ref_namespace(identity_namespace)),
            reclaim_policy=S3IdentitySpecReclaimPolicy.RETAIN,
        )
        self.credentials = S3Credentials(
            self,
            "credentials",
            metadata=ApiObjectMetadata(name=name, namespace=tenant),
            seaweed_ref=S3CredentialsSpecSeaweedRef(name=cluster.NAME, namespace=_seaweed_ref_namespace(tenant)),
            identity_ref=S3CredentialsSpecIdentityRef(name=name),
            secret_ref=S3CredentialsSpecSecretRef(
                name=secret.name,
                access_key_field=AWS_ENV_KEY_FIELDS.access_key,
                secret_key_field=AWS_ENV_KEY_FIELDS.secret_key,
            ),
            reclaim_policy=S3CredentialsSpecReclaimPolicy.RETAIN,
        )
        self.access_key = secret.key(AWS_ENV_KEY_FIELDS.access_key)
        self.secret_key = secret.key(AWS_ENV_KEY_FIELDS.secret_key)
        if tenant != seaweedfs_namespace.NAME:
            kinds = ["Bucket", "S3Credentials", *(["S3Identity"] if local_identity else [])]
            ResourceReferenceGrant(
                self,
                "grant",
                metadata=ApiObjectMetadata(name=f"{tenant}-{name}", namespace=seaweedfs_namespace.NAME),
                spec=ResourceReferenceGrantSpec(
                    from_=[ResourceReferenceGrantSpecFrom(group=_GROUP, kind=kind, namespace=tenant) for kind in kinds],
                    to=[ResourceReferenceGrantSpecTo(group=_GROUP, kind="Seaweed", name=cluster.NAME)],
                ),
            )

class PostgresBackup(Construct):

    the identity lives beside `db`, the bucket adopts an existing physical one of its name, 30-day
    retention, gzip, a base backup daily at 02:00 UTC."""

        self,
        scope: Construct,
        id: str,
        *,
        db: PostgresRef,
        bucket: str,
        secret_name: str | None = None,  # PrivateBucket's: a live Secret name to keep
    ) -> None:

            self,

            tenant=db.namespace,
            local_identity=True,
            adopt_existing=True,
            description=f"CNPG base backups and WAL of {db.name}.",

class AgentReadable(StrEnum):

class Vpa(StrEnum):
    """Goldilocks' VPA for the namespace. Its controller runs on-by-default (goldilocks.py:43), so every
    namespace it has not been told to skip gets a recommending VPA."""

    DISABLED = "disabled"
    RECOMMEND = "off"
    INITIAL = "initial"
    AUTO = "auto"


def namespace(
    scope: Construct, id: str, *, name: str, vpa: Vpa, agent_readable: AgentReadable | None
) -> k8s.KubeNamespace:
    labels: dict[str, str] = {}
    match vpa:
        case Vpa.DISABLED:
            labels["goldilocks.fairwinds.com/enabled"] = "false"
        case Vpa.INITIAL | Vpa.AUTO:

        case Vpa.RECOMMEND:

decisions.question: Relax the boundary 'no record type standing in for an object' (`cluster/cdk8s/AGENTS.md:8-13`) for identity-only references?
decisions.recommendation: Yes. Limit it to frozen dataclasses of names, keys, ports and labels that the producer declares (`SecretRef`, `SecretKey`, `Port`, `Pods`, `ServiceRef`, `HostNetworkServiceRef`, `PostgresRef`), projected by methods. A record describing what to build stays banned, and so does a map that chooses wiring; a map that checks it (`OPERATOR_CRDS`, `ORDERING_EXCEPTIONS`) is allowed.
decisions.tradeoff: Seven small types to learn, and import edges from consumers to producers, where cycles are avoided with leaf modules as `ssh_mcp/config.py` already does. Without them, cross-module facts stay re-spelled strings, and N7, N14 and N15 stay hand-wired on both sides.

decisions.question: Adopt #7094 as the governing Flux dependency policy: merge it, or fold rules 1, 2 and 4 into AGENTS.md?
decisions.recommendation: Merge it after one revision: rebase past #7441, which already removed the three-layer law it replaces; point rule 2's table at `flux.ORDERING_EXCEPTIONS`, checked at synth; note that derived Orphan covers the delete-or-rename case rule 3b keeps a narrow unit for; and refresh its numbers from devel aaaa3a5b90. Folding only rules 1, 2 and 4 into AGENTS.md would drop rule 3's unit boundaries and rule 6's shared-artifact ordering, which the folds and exceptions rely on.
decisions.tradeoff: #7094 is docs only and was last updated on 2026-09-17; its evidence (713 edges, 278 units) predates the consolidation wave, and its burn-down plan would track what the check's burn-down table also tracks. Folding the three rules keeps AGENTS.md the single place to read, at the cost of the reasoning behind rules 3 and 6.

decisions.question: Postponed by the owner. Flip `flux_kustomization`'s `wait` default from `True` to `None` and gate only admission targets?
decisions.recommendation: Yes. The 23 admission targets pass `wait=True`, or `health_check_exprs` where the object has no Ready condition (kubevirt, cdi; #7699). Health checks on the 24 other nodes that carry them go, and a synth-time rule keeps `wait` and health checks off every node no admission edge targets. This reverses #7690's `wait=True` policy.
decisions.tradeoff: A Kustomization goes Ready once its objects apply, so runtime faults surface through the workload alerts (`KubePodNotReady`, `KubeDeploymentReplicasMismatch`) and gatus, which already fire. In exchange, kustomize-controller stops parking a worker for `timeout` on each reconcile of a sick unit, and one fault stops cascading as `DependencyNotReady` down the graph. With `wait` off, the default `timeout` rarely binds, so no timeout decision is needed.

decisions.question: Postponed by the owner. Derive `deletionPolicy: Orphan` for every generated directory that renders a stateful (group, kind)?
decisions.recommendation: Yes. Audit the 22 unprotected Kustomizations first, and with them the HelmRelease directories whose chart holds the state (loki, mimir, matrix/synapse), which pass `deletion_policy=ORPHAN` explicitly because detection sees only generated kinds. A deliberately disposable cache passes `MIRROR_PRUNE` or `DELETE`. This is also what makes folding stateful objects into their component's unit safe (#7094 rule 3).
decisions.tradeoff: Removing a node no longer deletes its PVCs and databases. The cost is that an intentionally removed directory leaves objects to clean up by hand.

decisions.question: Widen external-creds to in-cluster sources (minted bearers, controller outputs), and replace the ESO-ServiceAccount stores and per-pair stores with one referent-auth store per source namespace?
decisions.recommendation: Yes. Migrate one source namespace per PR, with forgejo-images (34 consumer namespaces) last; `cluster/cdk8s/external_creds.md` § Scope changes to match. Consumers' edges to stores and credential suppliers already went (#8183, #8186, #8188), and the external-creds node gains an `external-secrets-operator` edge because its store now lives there.
decisions.tradeoff: Exact-name, roster-authorized reads replace whole-namespace ESO reads and hand-kept allowlists. Every consumer namespace needs an `external-creds-reader` ServiceAccount, and stores and bindings are renamed, which causes transient ExternalSecret errors during each switch.

decisions.question: Require every pod spec to state `automountServiceAccountToken`, as its own fleet rule that lands before any ServiceAccount conversion?
decisions.recommendation: Yes. Converting a `KubeServiceAccount` to cdk8s-plus turns the account's token off (`automount_token` defaults to `False`), and a Pod that states nothing then loses its token silently: tana-mcp's firebase resigner calls the API with it (`tana/firebase_resigner/resigner.py:216`). The rule lands before the secrets step converts any account. It reaches every chart only once the writer attaches fleet rules, which you deferred.
decisions.tradeoff: Every raw pod spec gains one explicit line (the attic rotator states `true`); cdk8s-plus workloads already render `false`. A violation found by the rule is fixed by stating today's effective value, so the rule itself changes nothing at runtime.

decisions.question: Tighten `pod_hardening` to require drop-ALL capabilities and `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` on every container, with exemptions named in `FleetExceptions`?
decisions.recommendation: Yes, as its own PR after the per-area `harden()` PRs, with the violations fixed or exempted.
decisions.tradeoff: A container that relied on default capabilities breaks at runtime unless it is exempted.

decisions.question: Replace required nodeAffinity with a nodeSelector at the 8 `attract_to_zone` sites?
decisions.tradeoff: Scheduling is the same, but the rendered diff is large and reviewers must recognize it as a no-op. Keeping affinity would need `place()` to emit affinity on raw and CRD pods too.

decisions.question: One refresh rule for minted secrets?
decisions.recommendation: `CreatedOnce` everywhere. Rotation is deleting the Secret.
decisions.tradeoff: The 3 DB-role mints lose their 8760h re-mint. If yearly rotation is wanted, `MintedSecret` gains a refresh keyword at that point.

decisions.question: SeaweedFS naming: one ResourceReferenceGrant per bucket named `<tenant>-<bucket>`, credential Secrets never renamed, and `local_identity: bool` in place of a free identity namespace?
decisions.recommendation: Yes. `PrivateBucket` derives `<bucket>-s3-credentials`, the spelling attic, forgejo and registry-cache already use. The eight consumers that spell it otherwise (six `-seaweedfs-credentials` Secrets, `authentik-db-backup-s3`, openclaw's volsync Secret) pass their live name, so no key pair changes. Existing identities stay where they are.
decisions.tradeoff: Grants are renamed, which is safe because Flux applies the new grant before pruning the old one. Credential Secret names stay mixed: unifying them would need the seaweed_operator skill's handoff per consumer (a new S3Credentials, then a consumer switch), because renaming `secretRef` in place makes the operator mint a new key pair and strands the old Secret.

decisions.question: Delete the 39 goldilocks `enabled: "true"` namespace labels, leaving `"false"` as the only per-namespace label?
decisions.recommendation: Yes, in the PR that routes namespaces through `namespaces.namespace(vpa=...)`. Goldilocks runs on-by-default (`goldilocks.py:43`), so the label adds nothing, and the required `vpa` keyword states the per-namespace decision that `check_goldilocks_explicit_decision` (`cluster/validation/checks.py:151-176`) exists to force. That check and `check_goldilocks_namespace_labels` (`checks.py:85-101`), which demands `"true"` beside a `vpa-update-mode` label, change in the same PR.
decisions.tradeoff: The explicit decision moves from a rendered label to a required Python keyword, so hand-written namespaces keep the check until they convert. It also depends on Goldilocks' on-by-default flag staying set.

decisions.question: Who owns flux-system's `external-creds-reader` ServiceAccount? Three sources apply it today.
decisions.recommendation: The external-creds chart. flux-system exists before any Kustomization, and a single owner stops prune fights.

decisions.question: Is Kyverno an admission prerequisite for the units whose kinds its `Fail` policies match?
decisions.recommendation: No. Kyverno's chart templates no webhook configurations; its admission controller registers them once it runs, so an object applied before Kyverno is admitted unchecked. Ordering only decides whether the two admission-only mutations (`default-revision-history-limit`, `default-vpa-requests-only`) reach an object's first version. The `restrict-agent-*` policies gate agents' own requests, which come after bootstrap. Keep the `kyverno-policies` edges its CRDs need (rule 1), and drop the Kyverno-only edges in their own batch.

method:
The proposal was made in five steps, each by independent agents that could read the repo and run cdk8s in a scratch environment:
- Inventory: ten parallel sweeps covered every shared helper, per-concern wiring, open PRs and your review comments since the cdk8s layer began, planned and foreseeable needs, and what cdk8s and cdk8s-plus actually allow from Python.
- Design: four designers each proposed a complete convention set from a different angle: construct-centric, values-first, an intermediate model, and consolidating what exists.
- Judging: three judges scored every proposal on every need through one lens each: feasibility in Python, fit with your stated preferences, and maintainability and migration cost. A synthesizer started from the best-scoring proposal and grafted in what the judges singled out.
- Verification: one agent per example tried to break it, and a critic checked the whole design against your original request.
- Revision: the Flux graph on `devel` was measured against the admission-only direction (#7094), and the conventions, matrix, decisions, migration and examples were revised to match.
- Refresh, after the five steps: the counts, cites and excerpts were re-measured on devel aaaa3a5b90 once the provider cleanup, the writer and the edge trims had landed. The examples keep their earlier synthesis at 85fb8d0d; E8 and E10 to E13 were also re-run on aaaa3a5b90.
The page is rendered by `cluster/docs/cdk8s_conventions/render.py` from `proposal.json`: `bb run //cluster/docs/cdk8s_conventions:render_bin`.

scorecard.proposal: A. Construct-centric: single-shot kind classes, L3 composites with typed outputs, pod-policy mixins, nodes that read a RenderedDirectory
B. Values forward: declared references, PodPolicy.apply over k8s.PodSpec, single-shot kinds, a to_json bridge in providers
scorecard.summary: The strictest no-mutation model, and it found the key CRD-embedding fact: a JSON patch into a CRD slot is filtered by the CRD whitelist, and a to_json override is not. But it forces the 20 fluent workloads onto raw bindings, its PodPolicy cannot express pods that need a token, evolve relies on getattr, and the lambda assignment fails ruff E731. Taken into the synthesis: (group, kind) stateful keys and named hardening exemptions.

scorecard.proposal: C. Facts model: frozen need records with one renderer each, an HttpService archetype, DirectoryFacts
scorecard.summary: The strongest roster and glue-absorption ideas, plus the real SandboxTemplate embed check. But it is the parallel specification PLAN.md F forbids, its per-namespace Tenant grant cannot be built where a namespace's S3 objects span charts (monitoring), and HttpService silently adds default-deny policies. Taken into the synthesis: the explicit token-mount decision, write_directory absorbing components and configMapGenerator entries, and the synth-time approval check.

scorecard.proposal: D. Consolidate: one existing mechanism per job, harden()/place(), fleet_rules.chart, roster-only secret copying
scorecard.summary: The base of this recommendation. It uses one existing mechanism per job, keeps the AGENTS.md boundaries, gives a disposition for every open PR, adds a pygohcl relation test, and has the lowest migration risk. Its weak spots were cross-module agreement (strings recombined, N15 hand-wired on both sides) and enforcement (fleet_rules.chart can be bypassed). The grafted references and writer-attached rules fix both.
